title: GitLab Inc.
text:
In June 2015, the company was changed to a United States corporation.[1]

The company participated in the YCombinator seed accelerator Winter 2015 program. By 2015, notable customers included Alibaba Group and IBM.[2]

In January 2017, a database administrator accidentally deleted the production database in the aftermath of a cyberattack, causing the loss of a substantial amount of issue data and merge request data.[3] The recovery process was live-streamed on YouTube.[4,5]

In April 2018, GitLab Inc. announced integration with Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) to simplify the process of spinning up a new cluster to deploy applications.[6]

In May 2018, GNOME moved to GitLab with over 400 projects and 900 contributors.[7,8]

In June 2020, KDE moved to GitLab with over 2,600 projects and 2,700 contributors.[9,10,11]

On August 1, 2018, GitLab Inc. started development of Meltano.[12]

On August 11, 2018, GitLab Inc. moved from Microsoft Azure to Google Cloud Platform, making the service inaccessible to users in several regions including: Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Sudan, and Syria, due to sanctions imposed by Office of Foreign Assets Control of the United States.[13] In order to overcome this limitation, the non-profit organization Framasoft began providing a Debian mirror to make GitLab CE available in those countries.[14]

In 2020 at the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, GitLab Inc. released "GitLab's Guide to All-Remote" as well as a course on remote management for the purpose of aiding companies interested in building all-remote work cultures.[15,16] In April, the company expanded into the Australian and Japanese markets.[17,18] By November, it was valued at more than $6 billion in a secondary market evaluation.[19]

In 2021, OMERS participated in a secondary shares investment in GitLab Inc.[20]

On March 18, 2021, GitLab Inc. licensed its technology to the Chinese company JiHu.[21]

On June 30, 2021, GitLab Inc. spun out Meltano, an open source ELT platform.[22]

On July 23, 2021, GitLab Inc. released its software Package Hunter, a Falco-based tool that detects malicious code,[23] under the open-source MIT Licence.

On August 4, 2022, GitLab announced its plans for changing its Data Retention Policy and for automatically deleting inactive repositories which have not been modified for a year. As a result, in the following days GitLab received much criticism from the open-source community.[24] Shortly after, it was announced that dormant projects would not be deleted, and would instead remain accessible in an archived state, potentially using a slower type of storage.[25,26]

In May 2023, the company launched the "GitLab 16.0" platform as an AI-driven DevSecOps solution. It contained over 55 new features and enhancements.[27]

In July 2024, Reuters reported that GitLab was exploring a potential sale after attracting acquisition interest, with cloud monitoring firm Datadog named as one of the interested parties.[28]

In 2026, GitLab Inc. had over 10 thousand paying customers paying at least 5000 $/year, an increase of 8 % year-on-year.[29]

### Fundraising

GitLab Inc. initially raised $1.5 million in seed funding.[2] Subsequent funding rounds include:

September 2015 - $4 million in Series A funding from Khosla Ventures.[30]

September 2016 - $20 million in Series B funding from August Capital and others.[31]

October 2016 - $20 million in Series C funding from GV and others.[32]

September 19, 2018 - $100 million in Series D-round funding led by ICONIQ Capital.

2019 - $268 million in Series E-round funding led by Goldman Sachs and ICONIQ Capital at a valuation of $2.7 billion.[33,34]

### IPO

On September 17, 2021, GitLab Inc. publicly filed a Form S-1 registration statement for the initial public offering of its Class A common stock.[35] The stock began trading on NASDAQ under the ticker "GTLB" on October 14, 2021.[36] The IPO raised $650 million for the company.[36]
